items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Hanmer opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we are gathering from today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishnaabe and Neutral People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share their land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Councillor Hanmer provided Council with a moment of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

Today we recognize our East and Southeast Asian neighbours and friends as they prepare for Lunar New Year on January 22. This celebration marks an important social and economic holiday for billions of people around the world.

We wish folks celebrating prosperity and good luck as you usher in the Year of the Rabbit; may you enjoy good food and time spent with loved ones! We are grateful for the diversity within this community. Our city is enriched by the presence and contributions made by East and Southeast Asian community members who bring culture, traditions and flavours from around the world to Waterloo. Council encourages everyone to support local entrepreneurs and to borrow resources from Waterloo Public Library to explore Lunar New Year traditions further.
Happy Lunar New Year to all who celebrate!

items.title: Order of Canada - Mayor’s Congratulations
notes: Mayor McCabe offered remarks and her congratulations to Dr. Donna Strickland and Paul Born for their appointment to the Order of Canada:

We live in a special place. Waterloo is home to two highly ranked universities and a college. We have a thriving business and technology community. We have non- profit and community organizations that are second to none. We have a thriving urban centre with award-winning architecture, unique shops, a vibrant arts and culture sector and fantastic restaurants.
All of this attracts some of the best and brightest talent from across Canada and from our neighbouring communities. They come to Waterloo to make their home and their careers here.

Tonight, we’re taking a few minutes to honour three of the best and the brightest of our community. On behalf of Council and staff, I’m honoured to welcome and to acknowledge our recipients from Waterloo to Council Chambers tonight. Paul Born, from Tamarack Institute and Dr. Donna Strickland, from the University of Waterloo are with us tonight. Dr. Feridun Hamdullahpur, who was the University of Waterloo's sixth president and vice-chancellor, is travelling and unable to join us tonight. Hopefully he can join us another time.

For clarification, Dr. Donna Strickland and Paul Born were named to the Order of Canada in 2019. However, they were only recently, because of Covid, able to accept their awards. I felt it important to ensure, to welcome them to Council chambers, that they know how honoured and excited we are as a city to have residents like them in our community. Thank you for accepting our invitation to join us tonight so that, on behalf of all of our 140,000 residents, we can recognize your achievements. I’ll briefly introduce them and then invite them to come to the front and provide a certificate, and then we’ll return to our regular Council.

So Paul Born: Paul has long understood that there is a direct correlation between people’s sense of community and their willingness to improve the conditions of those who live around them. He is a thought leader, founder of ground-breaking organizations, and an early pioneer in the field of community engagement and collective impact for good.
He is the author of four books, the co-founder of the Tamarack Institute and Canada’s foremost expert on intentional and purposeful community engagement.

Paul and his work have focused on working collaborative with community to reduce poverty, support youth and deepen community connectedness. His is a significant contributor to the reduction of poverty of approximately 1 million people in Canada, bringing poverty to the lowest level in our history.
Paul – Congratulations on your well-deserved honour.
Thank you for your contributions to our city and region, to Canada, the US and beyond. And thank you again, on behalf of those you have helped to lift out of poverty.

Dr. Donna Strickland needs no introduction. You would have to be living under a rock since 2018 if you didn’t know that she was awarded the Nobel Prize for Physics. She is a professor in the Department of Physics and Astronomy at the University of Waterloo and was awarded the Nobel Prize for developing chirped pulse amplification as a PhD student.

Together with her PhD supervisor, they published their Nobel-winning research in 1985. This discovery enabled further research into intense laser pulses - the most intense ever created. We recognize this research and how it was applied today in industry and medicine — including in laser eye surgery, and the machining of small glass parts for use in cell phones.

In addition to her numerous awards, Dr. Strickland was appointed as a Companion of the Order of Canada. This recognizes outstanding achievement and merit of the highest degree, especially in service to Canada or to humanity at large.
Dr. Strickland – thank you for finding time in your busy schedule to join us tonight. Thank you on behalf of Council, on behalf of our residents and certainly on behalf of our Country.
